q: The person who prohibits halaal is the same as the one who permits haraam.
It is Sunnat to walk one’s guest to the door of the house.
Beware of assumptions, for statements based upon them are most likely to be untruthful.
Barakat lies with your elders.

In the zill (shade) of the 'arsh (Throne), on the day there is no other zill, will be the man who leaves his home to trade and seek sustenance from Allah Ta’ala’s grace. He does this to prevent himself from asking of others and to provide for his family.
Planning is one half of life. Proper planning is essential for a fulfilling life.
Exchange gifts with one another for doing so increases affection and cleanses hearts of grudges and ill will.

Three people remain untouched by the trials and tribulations of this world and the hereafter: the person who offers sincere advice to Muslims, the person who guides towards good, the person who is content with Allah Ta’ala’s judgement and will.
All Creation is a family dependent on Allah The most beloved of all Creation to Him, therefore, is the one who benefits His family the most.
The person who provides water should be the last to drink.
When you meet someone from my Ummah, greet him with salaam and your hasanaat will greatly increase.
Sadaqah given in secret extinguishes Allah Ta‘ala’s anger.
IT am amazed by a person who desires worldly pleasures and all the while Death seeks him.
Speak (what is true and right) even though it may be bitter.
The betrayal is great when your brother believes you to be truthful about what you tell him [because it comes from you], and all along you are lying.
The honour of a home lies in sweeping it (keeping it clean).
Do not speak ill of Muslims behind their backs nor pursue their flaws.
Do not make a promise to your brother that you will not keep.
A Muslim is not permitted to sever relations with his brother for more than three days.

A man will not perfect his belief in Allah without five qualities: having faith in Allah Ta’ala, entrusting all matters to Him, submitting to His command, accepting His judgement gladly, enduring His trials.
A powerful person is not one who brings another to the ground. Truly powerful is he who controls himself when angry.
A wealthy person is not one who has an abundance of material possessions. Truly wealthy is he who is content with whatever he has and is not dependent on anyone.
A man does not open for himself the door that leads to begging, but Allah opens for him the door that leads to poverty.
A father has not given his child a better gift than good manners.
A vile companion is like a blacksmith fanning a fire with his bellows: even if he does not burn you with the sparks of his fire, his odour will certainly stay with you.
A Mumin is like a honeybee: it does not consume nor give except that which is pure and wholesome.
A Muslim is one from whose words and actions other Muslims remain unharmed.
If a person has been provided a means by which he has obtained his livelihood, he should remain committed to it.
He who conceals his brother’s faults, Allah Ta‘ala will conceal his faults in this world and the hereafter.
Allah takes responsibility for the livelihood of one who seeks knowledge.
A person slain while defending his family is a shaheed (martyr) as is a person slain while defending his faith.
He who believes in Allah Ta’ala and the Last Day (Day of Qiyaamat) should speak that which is good or remain silent.
He who believes in Allah Ta’ala and the Last Day should honour and be hospitable to his guests.
When a person controls his anger despite being able to express it, Allah infuses his heart with peace and faith.
When one of you walks towards a he should walk slowly and unhurriedly.
If a person looks at his brother with the intent of finding fault, Allah Ta’ala will regard him with anger in this world and the hereafter.
He, who looks through his brother's books [letters or any other text] without his permission, is as if he looks at hellfire.
A Mumin is a Mumin’s brother; he neither wrongs nor insults him.
A Mumin for another Mumin is like a structure whose various parts support one another. Like the parts of a structure, one Mumin supports and strengthens another.
Allah gift to a Mumin is someone in need at his door.
One of you notices a speck of straw in his brother’s eye but ignores the trunk of a date palm in his own. He notices the imperfections of but ignores significant ones in himself.
Patience is the grave of all flaws.
Show kindness to others’ children and you Your children will be shown kindness as well.
times of comfort and ease, and He will acknowledge you [with aid and assistance]
Poverty is undoubtedly a hardship, but a more severe hardship than poverty is illness of the body. And an even more severe hardship than illness of the body is illness of the soul.
Lasting happiness lies in seeing [one’s]

A person who approves of a certain group’s act is the same as the one who participates in that act with them. And when participating in an act that is Baatil (wrongful), a person commits two sins: the sin of carrying it out and the sin of approval.
Your livelihood seeks you so be at ease.
A person who listens to backbiting is himself one of those who backbite.
Generosity is giving before being asked. As for giving after being asked, it is either out of shame or fear of being criticised.
A man’s self-admiration is one among those who are jealous of his intellect. Those jealous of an intelligent person wish for the ruin of his intellect.
A man’s liberation is in the truth.
Amirul Mumineen was asked, “If a man was to be locked up in a house and left there, how would his livelihood come to him?” He replied, “In the very same way his death would.”
Some morsels are such that they prevent many more.
Do not complain about your illness [to anyone] except to the one who can provide you with a cure.
There can be no closeness [to Allah in doing good deeds that are not obligated if they harm those that are.
People will not neglect an aspect of their religion in order to deal with a worldly but Allah Ta’ala will bring upon them that is far worse.
wealth if it has taught you a lesson.
Speak gently and you will be loved.
A person does not confine something to his thoughts but it escapes through slips of his tongue and expressions of his face.
deserving of reward than a person who though capable of carrying out an immoral act, refrains from it. Indeed, such a person is nearly a firishtah.
He who is obstinate will perish.
When a person mends that which is between himself and Allah Ta’ala, Allah Ta’ala will mend that which is between him and others.
When a person considers small hardships to be great, Allah Ta’ala will bring upon him hardships that are [in fact] great.
When one’s own soul (conscience) is his advisor, Allah is his protector.
A person should never blame another for suspecting him of doing wrong if he places himself in positions in which he is vulnerable to accusation.
Bring forth what you possess, for through it, you will be known.
Running away from your own self (self- indulgence) is more beneficial than running away from a lion.
The deed dearest to Allah Ta’ala is that which is most consistent, even if small.
When someone distinguished from a community visits you, honour him.
Gladly accept Allah Ta’ala’s will and you will [truly] become a zaahid.
Perfect your you will live longer.
Completing an act of kindness is better than starting it. If you start an act of kindness, complete it.
Do good to the worthy and the unworthy. If a person is worthy, then he is deserving of that good. If a person is unworthy, then you are one who does good regardless.
The bane of generosity is extravagance.
The bane of speech is lying.
The bane of forbearance is foolishness.
The bane of munificence is recounting favours.
The bane of courage is oppression. Courage should not lead one to transgress the limits of what is just and right.
The bane of cleverness is conceitedness.
The bane of ‘ibaadat is listlessness.
The bane of knowledge is to forget.
Enquire about your neighbour before purchasing a house and about your companion before embarking upon a journey.
The dictation of good is better than silence. However, silence is better than the dictation of evil.
What most entitles people to enter is the taqwaa of Allah and good character.
Jealousy consumes hasanaat (good deeds)
Through the goodness of his character, a man attains the status of one dedicated to rozah and namaaz.

In all His justice and fairness, Allah Ta’ala that comfort and relief shall reside in faith and contentment. Likewise, He has determined that worry and sorrow shall reside in doubt and discontentment.
When the intention [behind is to obtain with aakherat]. However, when the intention is worldly, He refuses to grant aakherat.
A small number of deeds undertaken with knowledge and understanding amounts to a lot. However, a large number of deeds carried out in ignorance and without understanding amounts to little.
